component.name: WinDrop
component.summary: Run Windows programs in their own private environment

description.p: WinDrop makes a Windows program behave like a Linux application. Drop an .exe or .msi onto its window and it works out what the program needs, builds an environment for it, runs the installer, and adds the result to your menu.

Each program gets its own environment, with its own Wine prefix and its own copy of any Windows runtime it depends on. Nothing is installed system-wide, WinDrop never asks for root, and removing a program removes everything it created — no leftovers in your home directory, in Wine's shared prefix, or in your registry.

Graphics are translated through DXVK and VKD3D-Proton where they help, and programs that need an older version of Windows can be told to expect one. Where a program needs particular attention, WinDrop tries a series of environments and remembers the one that worked.

ul.li: Per-application Wine prefixes, with shared runtimes kept separately.
Automatic profile resolution, with a fallback chain that learns what worked.
DXVK and VKD3D-Proton translation layers, downloaded on demand.
Bubblewrap isolation, so a program sees its own prefix and nothing else.
Menu entries and icons, with one-click launch and removal.
A complete command line, including JSON output for scripting.
